visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A middle-aged man with short black hair and rectangular glasses, wearing a dark green long-sleeved button-down shirt, stands in the center of the frame within a well-lit indoor living room. He holds a blue ballpoint pen in his right hand and a small black remote control in his left, gesturing actively with both as he speaks. Behind him is a grey textured sofa and a large, stylized wall poster featuring a light brown cat with its mouth wide open in a yawn. The lighting is bright and even, likely from studio lamps. (2) The scene cuts to a full-screen graphic featuring a white background and a stylized map of Taiwan. Various colored icons representing different medical centers are scattered across the island, with corresponding text labels in Chinese listed on the left side of the screen. A small red triangular caution icon is placed over several locations. (3) The video returns to the man in the green shirt in the living room setting. He continues to gesture with the pen, pointing it toward the camera to emphasize his points. His facial expressions are animated, with frequent movement of the eyebrows and mouth. (4) A high-quality 3D medical animation appears, showing a rotating blue neon DNA double helix structure against a dark, slightly textured background. Small glowing particles float around the strands, emphasizing a technological or scientific theme. (5) The camera cuts back to the man who is now holding the pen horizontally and moving it in a rhythmic fashion to match his speech pace. The background remains the same living room environment with the cat poster. (6) A technical pie chart graphic is displayed on screen, showing a breakdown of relationship types within a database. The chart uses bright colors like pink, green, and orange, with numerical percentages and labels like 'Related 70.9%' and 'Indep. 29.1%' visible. (7) Returning to the primary speaker, he leans slightly forward, increasing the intensity of his hand gestures. The lighting remains constant, and yellow subtitles continue to scroll at the bottom of the frame. (8) A complex bar chart graphic appears, displaying 'AUC' values for various medical conditions. The bars are a dark red color, and the x-axis contains numerous Chinese labels for diseases, with a secondary line graph overlaid on top. (9) The final phase shows the man in a wider medium shot, still in the living room. He brings his hands together while concluding his speech, his expression shifting to a slight smile. The overall environment and lighting remain professional and consistent.
visual_base.text_narrative_log: (1) [Slogan]: 訂閱挺健康 掌握健康指南. [Variety]: 誕生!全球最大 漢人基因資料庫. [Subtitle]: 想靠DNA預測疾病風險. (2) [Subtitle]: 終於有機會了. (3) [Subtitle]: 因為全球規模最大的漢人基因與電子病歷資料庫來了. (4) [Subtitle]: 就在臺灣. (5) [Subtitle]: 基因醫學我們聽了很久. (6) [Subtitle]: 但全世界八成資料來自歐洲人. (7) [Subtitle]: 拿挪威人的資料算臺灣人的糖尿病風險. (8) [Subtitle]: 就跟站著尿尿一樣. (9) [Subtitle]: 不準啦. (10) [Subtitle]: 為了建立一套對大部分臺灣人以及全球14億漢人更有用的資料庫. (11) [Subtitle]: 中研院揪了全台33家大醫院一起入陣. (12) [Subtitle]: 這就是「臺灣精準醫療計畫 TPMI」. (13) [Subtitle]: 資料包含56萬人的血液樣本加電子病歷. (14) [Subtitle]: 還有他們加入計畫前5年的回溯資料. (15) [Subtitle]: 以及未來所有的就醫紀錄. (16) [Subtitle]: 讓科學家能「縱向追蹤」. (17) [Subtitle]: 從健康、發病到治療的全過程. (18) [Subtitle]: 但到底要怎麼分析這麼多資料. (19) [Subtitle]: 又能看出什麼名堂. (20) [Subtitle]: 這就是TPMI的正式出道作. (21) [Subtitle]: 兩篇論文剛剛同步上刊《Nature》. (22) [Subtitle]: 首先TPMI自己研發兩代基因晶片. (23) [Subtitle]: TPMv1跟TPMv2. (24) [Subtitle]: 這不是CPU. (25) [Subtitle]: 而是幫DNA「對獎」的讀卡機. (26) [Subtitle]: 我們的DNA 99.9%都一樣. (27) [Subtitle]: 而那0.1%的差異. (28) [Subtitle]: 就是讓每個人獨一無二、疾病風險高低的關鍵. (29) [Subtitle]: 對，就是命. (30) [Subtitle]: 命沒有「對」「錯」，只有版本不同. (31) [Subtitle]: 有人力氣大，有人流的汗會爆炸. (32) [Subtitle]: 基因晶片上刻了上百萬個微小的探針「誘餌」. (33) [Subtitle]: 是一小段人工合成的DNA. (34) [Subtitle]: 利用A黏T、C黏G的「互補配對」規則. (35) [Subtitle]: 只要把DNA樣本貼上「螢光標記」. (36) [Subtitle]: 再倒到晶片上. (37) [Subtitle]: DNA碎片就會去找100%互補的「誘餌」. (38) [Subtitle]: 最後雷射一掃，看哪個探針亮起來. (39) [Subtitle]: 就知道這套DNA是哪一版. (40) [Subtitle]: 但TPMI幹嘛自己做. (41) [Subtitle]: 啊不然咧. (42) [Subtitle]: 以前的晶片探針抓的是歐美人的通用版. (43) [Subtitle]: TPMI這兩款才能精準抓到漢人特有基因. (44) [Subtitle]: 做後續的全基因體關聯分析(GWAS). (45) [Subtitle]: 和表型體關聯分析(PheWAS). (46) [Subtitle]: 把DNA和疾病連起來. (47) [Subtitle]: 不過自幹晶片只是第一關. (48) [Subtitle]: 第二關是病歷. (49) [Subtitle]: 臺灣33家醫院有33種格式. (50) [Subtitle]: 有些還留著醫師手寫字跡. (51) [Subtitle]: 對，沒人看得懂. (52) [Subtitle]: 所以團隊開發一套專屬AI. (53) [Subtitle]: 識別「抽菸」「喝酒」「血壓偏高」等關鍵詞. (54) [Subtitle]: 把亂糟糟的病歷變成能分析的數據. (55) [Subtitle]: 破兩關，還有隱藏第三關. (56) [Subtitle]: 親戚. (57) [Subtitle]: 團隊發現資料庫裡高達70.9%的參與者在三等親的圈圈裡. (58) [Subtitle]: 欸，這問題很大. (59) [Subtitle]: 假設我們要找「A基因」跟「糖尿病」的關聯. (60) [Subtitle]: 發現100個糖尿病患，哇～通通都有A基因. (61) [Subtitle]: 兇手就是A基因. (62) [Subtitle]: 但但但，如果他們通通有同一個阿公呢. (63) [Subtitle]: 所以TPMI導入了像SAIGE、REGENIE等先進「混合效應模型」. (64) [Subtitle]: 在計算時自動把親戚關係「校正回歸」. (65) [Subtitle]: 留下跟疾病的真正關聯. (66) [Subtitle]: 才能在不刪掉7成樣本下，算出不失真的結果. (67) [Subtitle]: 總算，團隊開發出「多基因風險評分模型 PRS」. (68) [Subtitle]: 能將一個人基因裡多個「風險變異」疊在一起. (69) [Subtitle]: 算出他得某種病的機率. (70) [Subtitle]: 結果不得了. (71) [Subtitle]: 開發出超過105種疾病的模型. (72) [Subtitle]: 準確度當然也比歐洲版高. (73) [Subtitle]: 例如僵直性脊椎炎的準確率AUC高達0.812. (74) [Subtitle]: 數字特別漂亮. (75) [Subtitle]: 其他如牛皮癬 0.709、糖尿病 0.64、高血壓 0.61也都頗有參考價值. (76) [Subtitle]: 他們還拿去跟TWB(臺灣生醫資料庫). (77) [Subtitle]: UK Biobank(英國生物樣本庫)的東亞裔數據. (78) [Subtitle]: 以及美國NIH的All of Us計畫中的東亞裔數據做交叉驗證. (79) [Subtitle]: 證明自家模型預測英國或美國的東亞裔也同樣穩又準. (80) [Subtitle]: 不過先說. (81) [Subtitle]: 用基因算命僅供參考. (82) [Subtitle]: 想成為 No.1 Hero. (83) [Subtitle]: 不用靠個性，有決心就行.
